name: Ask, Don't Assume
description: Ask clarifying questions when requirements are ambiguous instead of making assumptions that may be wrong.
content:
# Ask, Don't Assume Rules

- When a requirement can be interpreted multiple ways, ask which interpretation the user intends before proceeding
- Don't assume the technology stack — ask what framework, language version, or tools the project uses
- Don't assume file locations or project structure — ask or explore before making changes
- When fixing a bug, ask if the user wants a quick fix or a proper refactor — the answer affects the approach
- Don't assume the user wants related changes — if they ask to fix X, don't also refactor Y unless asked
- When instructions say "improve" or "clean up", ask for specific criteria — vague goals lead to unwanted changes
- Don't assume error handling preferences — ask if they want exceptions, error codes, Result types, or something else
- Ask about testing expectations — unit tests, integration tests, both, or none for this change
- When adding a dependency, ask if the user has a preference for which library to use
- Don't assume naming conventions — check existing code patterns or ask the user directly
- If a task seems too large for one session, ask if the user wants to break it into phases
- When multiple valid approaches exist, briefly present options and let the user choose — don't pick silently
